enonce_markdown: A title must be placed in the middle of a table, above columns A to F. Which feature joins the cells A1 to F1 into one cell and centres the title?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Merging combines several selected cells into one cell; the Merge & Center button in the Alignment group of the Home tab does it and centres the content.

### Solution

**Merge & Center** (option b). Wrap Text only breaks a long text over several lines inside one cell, Freeze Panes keeps rows or columns visible when scrolling, and Format Painter copies a format from one cell to another.

enonce_markdown: A cell contains the value 0.256. How can it be displayed as 25.6% without changing the value stored in the cell?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The format changes how a value is displayed, not the value itself. The Percentage format multiplies the displayed value by 100 and adds the % sign; the number of decimal places is set separately.

### Solution

Apply the **Percentage format with one decimal place** (option d). With no decimal place the cell would display 26%, the Number format with one decimal place would display 0.3, and the Currency format would add a currency symbol and show 0.3.

choix.texte: The Percentage format with no decimal places
The Number format with one decimal place
The Currency format with one decimal place
The Percentage format with one decimal place

enonce_markdown:
The marks of five students are in C2 to C6: 38, 50, 72, 49, 65. The teacher wants every mark below 50 to be shown with a red background.

(a) Describe how to do this with conditional formatting.

(b) Which cells will be coloured?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Conditional formatting applies a format automatically to the cells that meet a rule. Select the range first, then create the rule.

### Solution

**(a)** Select C2:C6. On the Home tab choose Conditional Formatting, then Highlight Cells Rules, then Less Than. Type 50 as the value and choose a red fill, then click OK.

**(b)** Only the cells containing **38** (C2) and **49** (C5) are coloured. 50 is not less than 50, so that cell stays unchanged.

enonce_markdown: A long list of customers is printed on four pages. The column headings are in row 1 and must appear at the top of every printed page. What should be used?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Some settings only affect the screen and others affect the printout. Repeating a row on every printed page is a page setup option.

### Solution

**Print Titles, with row 1 set as Rows to repeat at top** (option a). Freeze Panes keeps row 1 visible on the screen but does not repeat it on the printed pages. Print Area only chooses which range is printed, and Fit to one page wide changes the scale, not the headings.

choix.texte: Print Titles with row 1 as Rows to repeat at top

enonce_markdown:
A student formats a customer list and meets three problems. For each one, give the cause and the correction.

(i) A cell in a narrow column displays ####### after the number 15000000 is typed.

(ii) The telephone number 0655123456 is typed in a cell and the cell displays 655123456.

(iii) A long address in B2 is cut off because C2 contains data.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A cell may display something different from what it contains. Column width, number format and text wrapping control the display.

### Solution

(i) The column is too narrow to show the whole number. Widen the column (double-click the border of the column heading) or reduce the font size.

(ii) The cell has the Number format, which removes a leading zero. Set the cell to the Text format before typing (or type an apostrophe before the number), so that the number is kept as typed.

(iii) A text longer than the column is hidden when the next cell is not empty. Widen column B or use Wrap Text so that the address is shown on several lines.

enonce_markdown: In a table in A2:D20, every whole row must be highlighted when the value in column D of that row is greater than 1000. The range A2:D20 is selected and a conditional formatting rule based on a formula is created. Which formula must be entered?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

In a formula-based rule, write the formula as it would apply to the first selected cell (A2). The column must be fixed so that every cell of the row looks at column D, and the row must be free to change so that each row tests its own value.

### Solution

`=$D2>1000` (option c): the dollar sign before D fixes the column, the row 2 is relative and becomes 3, 4, ... on the next rows. With `=D2>1000` the cell in column B would test E2, column C would test F2, and so on. With `=$D$2>1000` every row would test D2 only. With `=D$2>1000` the row is fixed to row 2.
